tips.comment: Harry's Girl had an amazing debut. There was a moment in which she was searching for room, but when she found it, she showed some amazing speed. I thought she didn't even like the track and that a flat track like York will be much more to her liking. Richard Hannon is in great form.

Was very impressive on debut on Wolverhampton's all weather track over 5f winning by 7.5L . Today will be a lot tougher but K.Burke's yard have won 2 of the last 3 renewals of this race when Got To Love A Grey & Pillow Talk both graced the winners enclosure .

Continuous has to be respected given his liking for York and proven stamina, having won the St Leger, but recent form is a worry and I'm not sure he'll be able to dictate here even in first time cheekpieces. He gets 5lbs from Rebels Romance but that rival is consistently posting pieces of form which outstrip anything else in this field including his Breeders Cup win and 4th in the Sheema Classic last time. Although unproven at this trip he's a strong stayer at 12f and with the ground quick has every chance of staying the extra 2f and showing his class in this field.

Continuous peaked at the end of his three-year-old year, winning here at York and following that with victory in the St Leger and 5th in the Arc. He has not been as good since then and flopped last time in Dubai, well behind Epic Poet. But first-time blinkers are tried, and they might spark a revival. He gets weight from the front two in the betting as his Group 1 win was back in 2023, and he could go close again as Aidan O'Brien's horses are outperforming.

Epic Poet seems a little overpriced here despite the tactical race scenario likely not suiting. This horse finished a close second behind Byzantine Dream, who went on to run a cracker in a Japanese Group 1. He finished third next time when not far behind Double Major, which is a Group 1 horse. Rebel's Romance could probably get away with the 2 miles here, as I'm expecting a very weak pace. At the prices, I think this is the correct play.

Salanca's win on the AW last time out was clearly something of a surprise when he beat genuine 100 rated horses. He races here off 98 and even the short head 2nd to Endless Victory last year in a hot race at HQ has plenty of clues that he's more than capable of winning this. Clearly that win last time out shows that this 4yo is still improving and there's so much superb collateral form that he simply can't be ignored at a generous looking 6/1.

Thunder Run ended last season with a very promising run at Ascot, and he'll surely build on that this season. He was quite poor on reappearance as he got tired quite quickly. I'm not sure why they decided to step him up in distance, but this horse could be out of handicaps sooner rather than later.

Drawn with the pace but unlikely to be too close and should be able to sit off. Winner and placed at this level, including win off 94 and 0.5L 3rd off 99. Decent season last season despite only winning one, had plenty of good runs in decent handicaps. Two good runs this season when keeping on well for 2nd over 1m and being beat 0.5L 2nd at Chester from stall 12, having sweated up and raced wide. Should be hitting peak fitness now and Easterby going to 18% SR. Plenty of pace from Thunder Run, Salamanca, and a couple others, and unlikely they'll be able to sustain it here over a CD where the bias heavily favors horses mid-held up. Also has strength advantage over the 4yos as they won't have matured fully until around August.

Zain Blue has saved his best for York, finishing 2nd behind Battle Cry in his maiden (that rival a Group 3 winner since), then 5th and 1st in two handicaps over C&D, winning from a mark of 83 in first-time cheekpieces. Headgear left off for his reappearance but now goes back on and he's just 2 lbs higher than his win here in September. Up in grade but looks fairly weighted and well drawn (stall 8) with Thunder Run going forward from stall 4. Yard are in decent form having had a few winners in the last couple of weeks.

The model I run suggests the value bet here is Financer. Quite big odds of 17 means not fancied in the early market. All horses have a reasonably similar RPR, but Financer's is the highest of the field. He does have an official ranking that's rock bottom, meaning he goes out carrying the least weight of the runners here over the slightly longer 1m 2f trip. Unfortunate draw in stall 10, but over this longer distance, it should be manageable. Over a stone in weight difference on good to firm ground, over 1m 2f trip might be telling by the finishing line.

Two runs this year for the 5yo mare, going close twice in decent races. She was ridden by a very inexperienced apprentice - just 9 starts under rules and no winners. She’s in good hands now. She was 2nd of 15 last Aug over this 10.5f C/D in a £52K handicap - fast ground - and has the ability to be a player in this £30K contest.

Both Glittering Surf's wins have come on the all-weather at Kempton, but she got up late to beat Bermuda Longtail by a length last time and should do so again, providing she is ridden more handily from her low draw.

Consecrated was very impressive on his first outing over 7 furlongs at Newbury just over 4 weeks ago. The form is already beginning to work out and although this is a step up into Listed class he could win again. He has got a massive stride and being by Frankel there could be a lot of improvement to come.
Crown Of Oaks looked unlucky in running when only managing 3rd place behind Point Of Contact last time at Newbury and should reverse that on six pounds better terms.

Four of the last six winners of this ultra-competitive handicap have been rated 90+, and there's only the top five in that bracket here. This is one of them, and the horse even gets a major jockey upgrade to William Buick. This horse showed a great attitude to beat Hammer The Hammer last year, and that horse has won all three races since. The second last time out when 'not reaching' the winner has the hallmarks of a horse that's going to improve when sent handicapping, and the trainer agrees since he uses Buick only in certain such situations and has a better strike rate with him than any other jockey.

Cape Sovereign is still a maiden but has not finished worse than 4th in six runs. It has been 2nd, beaten by less than a length in both runs so far this season, and is one pound ahead of the handicapper. It could go well from stall 1 against the far rail.

I'm looking for horses which come from the rear in these sprints because of there being a headwind and the pace often collapsing due to it. Just King High won from the rear at Southwell, which is quite rare. The trainer mentioned this horse needing fast ground, so you can scratch his run at Goodwood. 82 seems a fair enough mark.

A very open-looking sprint where King of Light looks a massive price at 28/1. He ran in a Group 3 last time and a listed event prior to that. Today's mark of 92 looks attractive, and he is well drawn in stall 14. The slight drop back in trip is another positive.
The Man was highly tried last season after winning on debut. He's making his handicap debut of 84, which could prove to be too low. Conditions will be in his favour.

The 3yo filly has 1 win from 7, but has been a runner-up twice and third also, unlucky in a few runs. Coming back from an 8 month break can see improvement and a change of luck. Her best run was probably a 3L defeat in a 15 runner Group 3 race, drawn on the wrong side and only losing out late on - runners at the front end from that race have since won two Group 3 races and two Group 2 races. After the early races up the far side at York this week, the near side - high draw could be advantageous with better unused ground. Her handicap mark of 86 looks very attractive. Top jockey K Shoemark takes the ride, and after the recent bad press, he’ll be keen to prove a point.

The model I run suggests Mum's Tipple can win this race. Mum's Tipple has the highest RPR of the field by quite a margin. Another large 22-runner field, this time over 7 furlongs. Mum's Tipple goes out carrying a middle-order weight here, with other current market leaders carrying slightly more. A previous course winner, so likes this track and a previous distance winner. Stall 5 and a good jump at the gate can help. Jockey on board claims a further 3 lbs, which is always helpful.

The model I run suggests Cooperation should win this one. Cooperation sets out with the highest RPR of the 9 runners here. Has a kind official ranking which means goes out carrying a reasonably low weight. Drawn in stall 1.

The model I run suggests Bedouin Prince should win this. Lines up with the highest RPR of the field by quite a way. Does carry a bit extra weight for the trouble but doesn't seem to be a big differential. Good prior form of 2-1 and drawn in stall 5. Stall draw doesn't tend to have a huge say at Newmarket given the course width, so stall 5 should be fine.

The model I run suggests Stacey Racey can win this race. Stacey Racey sets off with the highest RPR of the field and an official ranking of middle order. This leaves the weight being carried at a workable mark and therefore not really punished for the higher RPR. Last ran 22 days ago, so race fitness isn't a concern and came a reasonable 4th.

The model I run suggests Logi Bear can win this race. Logi Bear lines up with the highest RPR of the 11 runners. This race is for younger 2-year-olds with less data to judge on, but all go out carrying a very similar weight. Middle stall draw 8, which is ideal for this length of race, and over the 6f can look to go one better with form of 3,2.

The model I run suggests Speriamo can win this one. Not too fancied by the early market. Lines up with mid-rating RPR but does carry significantly less weight for this. Is a previous course and distance winner, so knows how to win. Form of 2, 2, 1, 3-5, so probably needed the last run from a previous break. Last run 13 days ago.

Gelded son of Dubawi & Dubai Beauty ( Dam's sire Frankel ) who has found himself an excellent opportunity here now this race is competitive but it certainly is an assignment that will suit Silent Age's nature of going perfectly well with his ideal pace level at his disposal given the horses enrolled to run here and ideal ground conditions he ticks all boxes to outrun his valuable E/W odds at the time of writing was last seen at Lingfield racing on the polytrack surface 28 days ago where finishing a creditable 7th/14 that was also his first attempt at the full 1 mile 2 furlongs trip and is most certainly worth another chance over this trip this time on the turf track here at Newbury which will play well into his strengths currently operating on a mark of 83 which is well within range Ian Williams's inmate can play a huge role in this class 3 handicap over on the business end with jockey Jim Crowley taking the ride that being a positive booking must be taken seriously and accordingly and mist certainly worth the E/W shout with some firms offering more than 3 places in this if you shop around

Form has been a bit up and down but has raced well here in the past, including a year ago gaining a creditable third off a mark 7lb higher than today. Now runs off lowest ever mark and whilst it's a while since last win, you feel it's coming. Seems a big price.

Good stable. This one showed promise in its first two runs when finishing 5th of 21 at Navan, beaten 15 lengths by Cast a Spell, recorded an RPR of 101, and then third of 20, beaten 1.75 lengths by Baby Kate at Navan, recorded an RPR of 112. Disappointed last time out when favorite, beaten 29 lengths by Coral River, did not act on the heavy ground. Looks the one to beat in this poor event.

This mares’ novice hurdle doesn’t look overly strong, and several are unexposed. Moonlit Mist is a useful flat winner and now makes a hurdles debut. The trainer, David H Kelly, has had success with similar types of horses and should be taken seriously here in a weak race. If the flat ability holds, she could be very dangerous if her jumping holds up.

Keep Kool Coko ran well above expectations when 6th in a strong Punchestown series final. He has proven ability in big field handicaps, now back into maiden company dropping in class. A definite win/place contender as his experience and form are both strong

Trained by Henry De Bromhead, who has a 22% strike rate at this track in the last year. Darragh O'Keefe takes the ride. Third on last run in a Kilbeggan Maiden Hurdle over 19 furlongs. Won a three-mile Point to Point before moving to current connections.

A couple of bad mistakes coming home on his latest outing when in contention, finishing 3rd of 14 over 2 miles, beaten 6 lengths. He had previously finished 3rd again, though a much closer 4 length difference, and that was the first outing this season in March from when last seen in December. He has a win on the flat and has come close with a runner-up last November. He is upped in trip for the first time, and that can make the difference. If avoiding his usual mistakes, I think he can win this.
Changed stables since last seen but won't take much getting ready. Probably best caught fresh. Has form to play a part if staying this longer trip on Irish return.

Was in good form over fences last autumn, coming 2nd numerous times and then finally getting his head in front at Wexford. Back over hurdles today off his timber mark, 16lb lower, and the booking of talented conditional Aiden Kelly, who takes a further 5lb. He's gotta go close, surely.

Flat winner who also scored over hurdles twelve months ago. An eight pounds rise subsequently made life difficult but assessor has gradually relented and Makfils now finds himself on a two pounds lower mark than for that Punchestown success. Cheekpieces are added to the often worn tongue tie, and the headgear together with his diminished handicap mark could trigger a return to his best.

This is a trainer's only entry he's got out today as they are returning it back to the hurdles with a good jockey booking/change. As this is his only ride of the day, it's a good value each way bet for the 5 places available.

Love Like This is a 7-year-old mare trained by the in-form John Patrick Ryan (won with 3 of his last 6 runners). She has yet to win over hurdles but deserves the breakthrough win, having placed 7 times from 18 starts over hurdles. She has finished runner-up twice in the last six starts, posting a near career-high RPR of 94 (todays good ground). Connections put up a 7lb conditional today in the shape of John Aherne, so she runs off 87. The trip doesn't present any problems, and she handles good ground. She is due her day in the sun!
Not shown much yet, but on better ground can improve. From a top in-form stable, the addition of cheekpieces for the first time could be the answer.
Lightly raced under National Hunt rules. Back up in trip. Could yet improve. Seven-pound claimer takes the ride. On a good mark.

Expound has won 3 times on the flat and once over hurdles last year at Tramore. He has won on the flat here at Clonmel and showed a welcome return to form when winning a 1m1f handicap at Ballinrobe last week. Good ground is ideal, and he has a good chance back over hurdles.

Ballycashin is a former winner at Clonmel (well-backed and ran out an easy six-length winner off a mark of 102 on this card last year but over 2m3f). Runs off a mark four pounds higher here, again follows a fair effort at Punchestown. Close to the foot of this handicap hurdle, Donagh Meyler rides the 8-year-old mare. Interesting having won easily here a year ago and has a fair chance in this company.

FASCINATING SHADOW gets back his ground and could be well laced well treated at the base of this weak looking handicap hurdle. He comes from a shrewd Irish source who place well and arriving on the back of an encouraging effort on the flat latest he can be expected to show up well.

This looks like a modest and open handicap hurdle, and my selection is Mountain Port. Tailed off at Punchestown on stable debut, but previous form was better and has won a maiden hurdle. With some improvement and now settled in, if stepping up here with past ability, definitely not ruled out at 33/1 today.
Useful mare finished in the frame on 5 of her first 6 outings , before finding Listed company too hot last time, Back down in grade and has an experience advantage over these rivals.
Ballyredinkingston recently ran a good 3rd in a Killarney bumper, showing some promise. He has the experience and a decent recent run under his belt so definitely one to consider for the win.

Carsons Dreamboat was a very poor 8th in one hurdle run 16 months ago. Seems bad, but after a long layoff and switching into a bumper race now, it comes from a good trainer and yard, Gordon Elliott. This helps the case and will be a dark horse if fitness is raring to go. EW shout.

Lightly raced and never put into his maidens but saw a markedly improved performance on handicap debut at Kilbeggan. Ridden much closer to the pace, was still a bit naive as he lost his position but stayed on to finish a close 2nd. Up in trip today, which is bound to suit, and with the excellent Darragh O'Keefe in the saddle, he could take all the beating. A mention for Shark's Qaasid, who will be of major interest next time as he was an eye-catcher in his maidens and looks well handicapped on that form.

Reverts back to hurdles after having been pulled up over fences last time. Had been shaping up well over fences but is well in here as his hurdles mark is a few pounds lower, so worth an each-way bet.

ZOLPHARINE has run well at this venue when fresh previously and he is no doubt a well treated handicap hurdler. He gets to take his chance with the yard aming the recent winners and those sired by Yeats often retain their ability as mature older types.

Trained by Pat Flynn and has 7 lb claimer PT Smithers on board. Had a flat prep run last time out at Dundalk over two miles. Prior to that, won a handicap hurdle at Wexford in fine style. Made headway from three out and kept on well to claim a short head victory. Each way claims.

Answering switches back to hurdles today after a fall over the bigger fences, and this will be safer, safer, and it suits him better. His form has been, let's say, 'variable,' but he is very capable of sneaking into the frame on his best day, and the odds are big enough for the EW play here.
